close_reason: Superseded by PKIX-amgn.5: dropped #![no_std] from pkix-lint-cabf/src/lib.rs as part of the cabf_tls_br module migration; added pkix-lint + pkix-profiles-cabf + x509-cert + der to [dependencies] in pkix-lint-cabf/Cargo.toml; replaced stale 'Stub crate' rustdoc section with current Modules description. Acceptance criteria of .5.1 (no_std removed, deps added, cargo check clean) all met by .5's commit c70821b4. The 'design question' (std vs no_std) was resolved per .5.1's own recommendation: std posture, matches pkix-lint, no current no_std consumer use case.
description:
## Why

The current `pkix-lint-cabf` stub declares `#![no_std]` at `pkix-lint-cabf/src/lib.rs:46`, but the `cabf_tls_br.rs` content scheduled to move into it (PKIX-amgn.5.2) currently uses `std::sync::OnceLock` and `std::error::Error`. The crate must pick a posture before the move.

## What

1. Decide std vs no_std. Recommendation: drop `#![no_std]` — pkix-lint itself is std (it has the oscal feature which requires serde_json + std), and the moved code uses std primitives. There is no consumer use case for a no_std CA/B Forum lint bundle today.
2. Update `pkix-lint-cabf/src/lib.rs`: remove `#![no_std]` attribute. Keep `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, `#![deny(rust_2018_idioms, unreachable_pub)]`, `#![warn(missing_docs)]`.
3. Add to `pkix-lint-cabf/Cargo.toml`:
   - `pkix-lint = { workspace = true }` (or path-relative if workspace inheritance not yet wired)
   - `pkix-profiles-cabf = { workspace = true }`
   - `x509-cert = { workspace = true }`
   - `der = { workspace = true }`
4. Update the rustdoc on `pkix-lint-cabf/src/lib.rs` to drop the "Stub crate" status note in preparation for substantive content (PKIX-amgn.5.2).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `#![no_std]` removed from `pkix-lint-cabf/src/lib.rs`.
- [ ] Cargo deps added; `cargo check -p pkix-lint-cabf` clean.
- [ ] No source code moves yet (.2 does that); no behaviour change to other crates.

## Out of scope

- The actual cabf_tls_br.rs move (PKIX-amgn.5.2).

## Design question (human approval)

Std posture: confirm flip to std. Recommendation is std for the reasons above; if there is a use case for no_std CABF lints in PKIX-amgn.5.x's broader timeframe, file a separate bead.
notes:
Escalating to human (2026-05-11): bead explicitly designates a "Design question (human approval)" gate on the std-vs-no_std decision. The bead's own recommendation is to drop #![no_std]:

- pkix-lint itself is std (oscal feature requires serde_json + std).
- The cabf_tls_br.rs content scheduled to move into pkix-lint-cabf in PKIX-amgn.5.2 uses std::sync::OnceLock and std::error::Error.
- No consumer use case for a no_std CA/B Forum lint bundle is on file.

I concur with the recommendation. Three lower-risk alternatives I considered and rejected:

1. Keep no_std and gate cabf_tls_br.rs body behind a "std" feature. Rejected: the entire reason to have pkix-lint-cabf is to ship the CABF rule encodings; gating them behind a feature flag is "stub by another name" and forces consumers to think about an axis (no_std CABF) that nobody is asking for.

2. Migrate the std::sync::OnceLock callsites to once_cell::sync::Lazy + add once_cell as a workspace dep. Rejected: adds a new workspace dep purely to preserve a no_std posture no consumer needs. Inverted cost/benefit.

3. Move cabf_tls_br.rs into pkix-lint-cabf as #[cfg(feature="std")] gated and leave the lib.rs as no_std. Rejected: dead-on-arrival shape — pkix-lint-cabf with the std feature off has no public content whatsoever, since the bundle IS the std-only material.

Awaiting human confirmation. Once confirmed, the bead is straightforward — remove #![no_std], add the four workspace deps, update lib.rs rustdoc, cargo check.
title: Decide pkix-lint-cabf no_std posture and update crate skeleton
